header: University of Texas at Arlington, Arlington, Texas, United States
profile: Jamila Javadova-Spitzberg is an assistant professor at the University of Texas at Arlington, where she teaches organ and harpsichord. She holds a Doctor of Musical Arts degree in performance from the University of North Texas (2008), a Master of Music from the Azerbaijan State Conservatory (1986), and further qualifications from the Conservatorium van Amsterdam, the Associated Board of the Royal Schools of Music, and the Leopold Mozart Center in Augsburg. She performs on organ, harpsichord, and historical fortepiano, and in 2017 she founded the Azerbaijan-American Music Foundation, of which she is executive director. In 2022 she received the Tarraggi Medal of the Republic of Azerbaijan.

He has more than 96 articles, nearly 100 patents, three books in Japanese, and more than 15 book chapters.

profile: Varga Kalantarov is professor in the Department of Mathematics at Koç University in Istanbul, where he has worked since 2001. He received a Doctor of Sciences in differential equations and mathematical physics from the V. A. Steklov Institute of Mathematics at St. Petersburg in 1988. The dissertation is Global behavior of solutions of nonlinear equations of mathematical physics of classical and non-classical types. He received a PhD in the same field in 1974 from the Institute of Mathematics and Mechanics of the Academy of Sciences of Azerbaijan. The dissertation is On mixed problem for semi-linear parabolic-hyperbolic systems. He studied at Azerbaijan State University in 1966–1971. From 1989 to 1993 he headed the Department of Partial Differential Equations at the Institute of Mathematics and Mechanics in Baku and was deputy director of the institute in 1984–1993.

header: Royal Conservatory of Music and Art, Muscat, Oman
profile: Saida Khalilova is founder and director of the Royal Conservatory of Music and Art in Muscat, a post she has held since November 2023, and an associate professor at the Baku Music Academy since October 2011. She received a PhD in music pedagogy from the Baku Music Academy in 2014 and a Master of Arts in music there in 1996. She taught piano at Sultan Qaboos University from 2011 to 2018 and at music colleges in Baku and Shusha. Her publications include a 2016 book and several papers on Elmira Aliyeva and piano education in Azerbaijan. She has developed more than 20 programs and served as author and artistic director of about 20 projects, competitions, and concerts, with appearances at the embassies of Japan, Turkey, France, and Russia.

header: Institute of Turkish World Studies, Ege University, Izmir, Turkey
profile: Vefa Kurban is a professor at the Institute of Turkish World Studies of Ege University. She received a doctorate in the history of the Republic of Turkey from Ege University on 26 March 2007. The thesis is urbanization and settled life in Azerbaijan between 1900 and 1978, supervised by Tuncer Baykara. Her master’s thesis, on land ownership in Azerbaijan in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, was completed on 23 June 2000. Her bachelor’s degree in history is from Ege University, dated 3 September 1997. She was an associate professor at Izmir University of Economics from 2007 to 2019 and at Ege University from 2015 to 2019.

header: Massey College, University of Toronto, Toronto, Canada
profile: Reza Moridi is a senior fellow of Massey College at the University of Toronto, a post he has held since 2020. He was Ontario’s Minister of Research, Innovation and Science in 2014–2016 and Minister of Training, Colleges and Universities, and he sat in the Ontario parliament for Richmond Hill from 2007 to 2018. He received a PhD in physics from Brunel University in 1975, an MTech in semiconductor physics and technology there in 1972, an MSc in nuclear physics from the University of Tehran in 1968, and a BSc in physics there in 1966.
